title: Kinetic Energy Proportional to Velocity Squared
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: The kinetic energy K of a moving mass is proportional to the square of its velocity v. If K = 12,960 joules when v = 18 m/sec, what is K when v = 10 m/sec?

steps.title: Formulate the Proportionality Model
steps.explanation: Since kinetic energy K is proportional to the square of velocity v, we write K = kv^2 for a constant k.
steps.why: In classical mechanics, K = (1/2)mv^2 has constant proportionality factor k = m/2 for a fixed mass.

steps.title: Find the Proportionality Constant k
steps.explanation: Substitute K = 12,960 and v = 18 into K = kv^2. Since 18^2 = 324, dividing 12,960 by 324 gives k = 40 J/(m/s)^2.
steps.why: Dividing the known energy by the square of the known speed isolates the constant k.

steps.title: Evaluate K at v = 10 m/sec
steps.explanation: Substitute k = 40 and v = 10 into K = 40v^2 to obtain K = 4000 joules.
steps.why: Once k is known, the formula K = 40v^2 determines K for any velocity v.
